title: Nut-Free Vanilla Latte Cupcakes
shortDescription: Coffee-infused vanilla cupcakes with a swirled vanilla buttercream, ready in about 45 minutes with 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake time.
description: These cupcakes taste like your favorite morning latte in cake form. The batter gets its coffee flavor from real espresso, mixed right into a soft vanilla base. I tested this recipe in my home kitchen using instant espresso powder, so no special equipment is needed. The crumb stays gentle and moist, not bitter or sharp. A plain vanilla buttercream on top balances the coffee note without fighting it. This recipe is nut-free, so it works for school bake sales or office treats. No nut flours, extracts, or garnishes touch this batter or frosting Swirl the two flavors together if you want a true latte look, or keep the frosting solid vanilla for a cleaner finish.
ingredients: 2 tbsp instant espresso powder dissolved in 2 tbsp hot water, cooled
instructions: Preheat your oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
In a medium bowl, whisk the flour, baking powder, and salt together. Set aside.
In a large bowl, beat the butter and sugar until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add the eggs one at a time, then mix in the vanilla extract.
Add the flour mix in three parts, alternating with the milk. Mix just until smooth.
Stir in the cooled espresso mixture until the batter turns a light coffee color.
Divide the batter evenly among the liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack.
For the frosting, beat the softened butter until smooth. Add powdered sugar, vanilla bean paste, and heavy cream, then beat on high for 2 minutes until fluffy.
Pipe the frosting high on cooled cupcakes using a large open star tip. Dust lightly with extra instant espresso powder if you like a stronger coffee look.
tips: Cool the espresso mixture fully before adding it to the batter, or it can melt the butter structure and thin the mix.
Swap in decaf instant espresso powder if you want the flavor without the caffeine.
For a true latte swirl, split the frosting in half and tint one half with a teaspoon of the espresso mixture, then pipe both colors together in one bag.
Store cupcakes in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days, or refrigerate for up to 5 days.

faq.question: How much caffeine is in each cupcake?
faq.answer: Each cupcake has a small amount, roughly what you would get from a few sips of coffee. Use decaf instant espresso powder if you want to skip the caffeine completely.

faq.question: Can I make these ahead of time?
faq.answer: Yes. Bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store them unfrosted in an airtight container. Frost them the day you plan to serve them for the best texture.

faq.question: Why did my batter turn out gray instead of light coffee colored?
faq.answer: This happens when the espresso mixture is too strong or added while still hot. Use exactly 2 tablespoons of espresso powder and let the mixture cool before mixing it in.

faq.question: Can I use brewed coffee instead of instant espresso powder?
faq.answer: Brewed coffee works but gives a weaker flavor and adds extra liquid. If you use it, reduce the milk by 2 tablespoons to keep the batter from getting too thin.

conclusion: These cupcakes bring coffee shop flavor to a nut-free bake, so anyone can enjoy them without worry. The soft crumb and gentle coffee note make this a easy pick for morning gatherings or afternoon coffee breaks.
